project.name: ree-v3
project.description: REE V3 is the active implementation substrate for the Reflective-Ethical Engine (REE), a research programme where architectural claims become experiments over predictive-context, self-relevant forward modelling, harm modelling, commitment and offline integration systems. nodes.languageNotes: Pure-Python stdlib arithmetic (no torch, no nn.Module inheritance); accepts torch tensors defensively via getattr/hasattr and coerces to a Python list before per-scalar EMA math.

nodes.name: ConditionedSafetyStore
nodes.summary: EMA-prototype conditioned safety predictor for SD-051 / MECH-304: learns which z_world states predict suffering absence via MECH-302 relief events (encoding pathway) and emits a sigmoid(cosine)-based safety_prediction scalar (expression pathway). Optional SD-066 centered mode subtracts a slow common-mode baseline before matching so a small cue residual can dominate under SD-008 z_world under-differentiation. MECH-094-gated: simulation ticks never advance the prototype.
nodes.languageNotes: Prototype + optional baseline held as plain Python lists updated in place; supports both raw-cosine and SD-066 centered-residue readouts under a single gain-adjusted sigmoid.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Configures the safety store: world_dim, EMA / decay / gain / threshold knobs, and the SD-066 centered-mode toggle plus its baseline_alpha. Initialises the prototype vector, the optional common-mode baseline, and internal counters (n_events, has_prototype).

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Waking-path tick: coerces the incoming z_world into a plain list, optionally advances the SD-066 common-mode baseline EMA (skipped in centered-mode when sim_mode is set), applies per-step L2 decay toward zero, and on a MECH-302 event tick blends the (centered or raw) z_world into the prototype via ema_alpha. Returns the current safety-prediction scalar via _query. Under sim_mode returns 0.0 with no state change (MECH-094).
nodes.languageNotes: Defensive tensor coercion (detach/squeeze/tolist) keeps the class torch-free while accepting torch inputs; L2 decay + EMA implemented as scalar list comprehensions.

nodes.name: _query
nodes.summary: Internal read: returns 0.0 when the prototype norm is below min_norm (no learned cue yet); otherwise computes cosine similarity between the query vector and the prototype and maps it through a scaled sigmoid (gain * cos) to produce the safety_prediction scalar in [0,1].

nodes.name: e2_world_uncertainty.py
nodes.summary: SD-063 E2 conditional predictive-uncertainty head over (z_world, action): a distribution-free quantile network with online pinball-loss training, replay buffer, and predictive std / variance readouts that feed ARC-016's dynamic commit-precision gate.
nodes.languageNotes: Quantile/HL-Gauss / pinball design with online mini-batch training, careful CPU-only Adam construction on first use to avoid pre-move device drift.

nodes.name: E2WorldUncertaintyConfig
nodes.summary: Config dataclass for E2WorldUncertaintyHead: master switch, network dimensions, quantile levels, online training knobs (learning rate, replay capacity, batch size), and readiness threshold.

nodes.name: E2WorldUncertaintyHead
nodes.summary: SD-063 quantile head: MLP trunk producing per-dim quantile logits over configurable levels, pinball-loss training on a rolling replay buffer of (z_world_prev, action, z_world_next) triples, and predictive-std / variance readouts scored against ARC-016 precision floors for E3.

nodes.name: forward
nodes.summary: Runs the trunk MLP on the concatenated (z_world, action) input and reshapes the output into [B, z_world_dim, Q] quantile logits.

nodes.name: compute_loss
nodes.summary: Standard pinball / quantile-regression loss: max(lv*err, (lv-1)*err) averaged over batch, dims, and quantile levels for the predicted vs realised next z_world.

nodes.name: _ensure_optimizer
nodes.summary: Lazily constructs the CPU-only Adam optimiser at first training-step invocation, avoiding stale parameter references after device moves.

nodes.name: train_step
nodes.summary: One online SGD step on a single (z_world_prev, action, z_world_next) triple: shape/dtype normalisation, pinball forward+backward, optimiser step, training counter increment.

nodes.name: observe_transition
nodes.summary: Appends a detached (z_prev, a, z_next) triple to the rolling replay buffer, then draws a mini-batch and runs one train_step; consulted from the agent's E2 tick.

nodes.name: get_state
nodes.summary: Returns a diagnostics dict (train step count, observed transitions, replay capacity/size, readiness threshold, ready flag, quantile levels) for manifest logging.

nodes.name: predictive_std
nodes.summary: Reads the per-input predictive standard deviation as the sorted quantile IQR converted via a Gaussian-reference factor, averaged over dims.

nodes.name: predictive_variance
nodes.summary: Per-input predictive-variance readout (std^2, monotone rearranged for anti-crossing) with per-batch and per-dim diagnostics; the value ARC-016's dynamic commit-precision gate consumes.

nodes.name: mel_consumer.py
nodes.summary: Implements the SD-MEL-CONSUMER substrate: an adaptive sleep-cadence Model Error Load (MEL) consumer that reads accumulated waking E3 prediction error and modulates sleep-phase duration (SWS/REM step scaling) and entry timing based on learning demand. Includes a Process-S time-integrating entry-pressure accumulator (SD-SLEEP-ENTRY-PRESSURE) fixing V3-EXQ-933.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses dataclass config pattern with mirrored REEConfig knobs; pure-arithmetic regulator with no learned parameters or nn.Module inheritance.

nodes.name: phase_manager.py
nodes.summary: Defines SleepLoopManager, the deterministic K-episode driver for the SD-017 sleep cycle that orchestrates the SleepPhase FSM (WAKING -> SWS_ANALOG -> PHASE_SWITCH -> REM_ANALOG -> WRITEBACK). Coordinates Phase B-E consumers (MEL, replay sampler, routing gate, Bayesian/self-model aggregators, cross-module consolidator) and supports MECH-286 override-gated entry and GAP-9 within-life triggers.
nodes.languageNotes: Large orchestrator (851 lines) using TYPE_CHECKING for forward references to sibling sleep-cluster modules; welfare_relevant marker denotes pre-ethical descriptive tag, not a gate.

nodes.name: MELConsumerConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding knobs for the MEL consumer (gain, reference, EMA alpha, duration factor min/max, entry-pressure gain/threshold). Mirrored onto REEConfig for from_dims wiring.

nodes.name: WakingMELAccumulator
nodes.summary: Rolling accumulator computing the mean per-step waking E3 prediction error (MEL) across a wake window. Guards against non-finite inputs and matches the V3-EXQ-701c instrument convention.

nodes.name: EntryPressureAccumulator
nodes.summary: Process-S-style time-integrating running-sum accumulator of per-step waking demand used for the SD-SLEEP-ENTRY-PRESSURE entry-timing lever. Grows monotonically with waking steps; discharged on cycle completion so sustained sub-threshold demand crosses in bounded time.

nodes.name: MELConsumer
nodes.summary: Main MEL consumer that reads waking prediction error and produces relative novelty, duration-factor scaling for SWS/REM step counts, and entry-timing signals (need_crossed / entry_pressure_crossed / entry_permitted). Publishes metrics for cycle_history and honors MECH-094 by writing nothing to memory outside waking.

nodes.name: SleepPhase
nodes.summary: Enum defining the canonical sleep-cycle phase ordering (WAKING, SLEEP_ENTRY, SWS_ANALOG, PHASE_SWITCH, REM_ANALOG, WRITEBACK) shared across the sleep-aggregation cluster (Phases A-E).

nodes.name: SleepCycleState
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding per-cycle bookkeeping: cycle_index, current phase, episodes_since_sleep, GAP-9 steps_since_sleep counter, and last_metrics. Reset at the start of each sleep cycle.

nodes.name: SleepLoopManager
nodes.summary: K-episode driver for the SD-017 sleep cycle. Advances SleepCycleState through the phase FSM, integrates MEL-driven duration scaling and entry-pressure triggers, routes replay draws through the MECH-272 routing gate, updates Bayesian and self-model aggregators, and invokes cross-module consolidation and REM precision recalibration.
nodes.languageNotes: Composes many optional consumers via constructor injection; carries a `welfare_relevant` marker as a descriptive SENT-0 tag, not a runtime gate.

nodes.name: phase3_preflight.py
nodes.summary: Preflight verification script for the Phase-3 coordinator/runner cutover — inspects environment config, schema readiness, hub sync mode, fleet lifecycle state, and machine identity, then emits a staged pass/fail verdict before workers or writers are allowed to modify the coordination plane.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Python dataclasses for structured check results, subprocess for SSH probes, urllib for HTTP checks, and argparse for CLI staging. Read-only diagnostic — never mutates coordinator state, matching the preflight-guard convention.

nodes.name: CheckResult
nodes.summary: Immutable dataclass carrying a single preflight check's identifier, category, pass/fail status, human-readable message, optional detail, and blocking flag — the atomic unit aggregated into the final verdict.

nodes.name: _load_env_file
nodes.summary: Parses a KEY=VALUE .env-style file into a dict, skipping blank lines and comments — the entry point for coordinator credential and endpoint configuration.

nodes.name: _ssh_run
nodes.summary: Executes a remote command over SSH with timeout, honouring dry-run mode; returns (exit_code, stdout, stderr) for downstream check evaluation.

nodes.name: _http_get
nodes.summary: Fetches JSON from an authenticated coordinator HTTP endpoint, returning parsed body or an error string — used by the hub /shadow/status probe.

nodes.name: _run_check_shadow
nodes.summary: Invokes the bundled check_shadow.py helper via subprocess to run coordinator shadow-mode diagnostics, capturing its line-oriented output.

nodes.name: _import_sync_daemon_ready
nodes.summary: Best-effort import of sync_daemon and confirmation that phase3 writer symbols exist — a compile-time gate proving the deployed daemon build carries the writers Phase 3 depends on.

nodes.name: _observed_sync_mode
nodes.summary: Normalises the coordinator's raw sync-mode string (dual/coordinator/git-only) into the canonical observed-mode enum used by stage resolution and hub verdict evaluation.

nodes.name: _resolve_stage
nodes.summary: Reconciles an explicit --stage flag against the observed sync mode and writer-ready state to pick the effective cutover stage (pre-cutover, dual, coordinator-only), recording where the final choice came from for the report.

nodes.name: _evaluate_hub_sync_mode
nodes.summary: Judges whether the hub's observed sync mode is legal for the chosen cutover stage and whether the operator pinned it correctly, producing a CheckResult with detailed disagreement reasoning when mode and stage mismatch.

nodes.name: _evaluate_fleet_lifecycle
nodes.summary: Walks per-machine lifecycle records from the coordinator, resolves canonical machine identities (guarding against the DLAPTOP hostname-drift class), and flags any machine whose lifecycle_state is not a known-good value — the fleet-side readiness gate.

nodes.name: run_preflight
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the full preflight sweep — reads env config, executes SSH/HTTP probes, calls the shadow-check helper, imports the sync daemon, resolves the effective stage, evaluates hub sync mode and fleet lifecycle — accumulating CheckResults into a single verdict payload.

nodes.name: _summary
nodes.summary: Rolls a list of CheckResult objects into a summary dict — counts pass/fail, isolates blocking failures, embeds the resolved stage, and stamps a UTC timestamp for the final report.

nodes.name: _verdict_lines
nodes.summary: Renders the summary dict into human-readable verdict lines describing overall pass/block state and per-category outcomes, formatted for direct terminal output.

nodes.name: _print_report
nodes.summary: Prints the full preflight report — header, per-check lines, and the aggregated verdict — to stdout in the human-facing report mode.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point — parses argparse arguments (env file, stage override, dry-run, mock, quiet, JSON output), invokes run_preflight, and emits either JSON or a human report, exiting non-zero when blocking checks fail.

nodes.name: task_claim_chip_git_writer.py
nodes.summary: Hub-only materialiser: renders the coordinator DB's task_claims + chips + workspace_state_entries (PHASE-4) + recommendation_log_entries spools into their git-tracked shapes (TASK_CLAIMS.json, TASK_CHIPS.json, WORKSPACE_STATE.md, decision-log JSONL) and commits with phase2b:/phase4: prefixes on state change. THE single git writer for these files since the 2026-08-28 cutover.
nodes.languageNotes: State-change-only commit gate via _texts_match + _semantic_delta so telemetry writers don't churn git history; last_rendered_json writeback provides the 3-way-merge base the next ingest cycle needs to preserve concurrent field-level edits.

nodes.name: _fetch_and_resolve
nodes.summary: Fetches origin and resolves the target branch's tip commit for the writer's rebase-onto step.

nodes.name: _parse_iso
nodes.summary: Parses an ISO-8601 timestamp string into a UTC datetime, tolerating trailing Z.

nodes.name: _source_order
nodes.summary: Deterministic key for ordering rendered entries (session_id + claimed_at, chip_ref) so the materialised file is stable across runs.

nodes.name: render_task_claims
nodes.summary: Renders the coordinator DB's task_claims table into the git-tracked TASK_CLAIMS.json shape, applying the >24h done-entry retention filter and ordering rows deterministically. The ONE git writer for TASK_CLAIMS.json since the 2026-08-28 cutover.

nodes.name: render_chips
nodes.summary: Renders the coordinator DB's chips table into the git-tracked TASK_CHIPS.json shape. Sister renderer to render_task_claims; both drive the git-write half of the PHASE-2b coordinator-authoritative registries.

nodes.name: _ws_render_guards
nodes.summary: Precondition/guard checks applied before rendering the WORKSPACE_STATE.md spool into the shared file (PHASE-4): confirms writer identity, checks for concurrent edits, refuses on conflicts.

nodes.name: render_workspace_state
nodes.summary: Drains the workspace_state_entries spool table (PHASE-4) and appends new entries to WORKSPACE_STATE.md, then marks them materialised via db.mark_workspace_state_entries_materialized. Idempotent by construction.

nodes.name: render_recommendation_log
nodes.summary: Drains the recommendation_log_entries spool table and appends new entries to the decision-log JSONL file, then marks them materialised. Idempotent.

nodes.name: ingest_dispatcher_control
nodes.summary: Reads the dispatcher-control side file (operator-authored knobs) and returns the parsed control payload for consumption by the render pass.

nodes.name: render_dispatcher_control
nodes.summary: Renders the coordinator's view of the dispatcher-lease state back into the dispatcher-control side file so operators see the live lease view.

nodes.name: ingest
nodes.summary: Umbrella ingest phase: pulls the current git-side JSON documents into memory so the writer's 3-way merge can compare against last_rendered_json.

nodes.name: _writeback_rendered_base
nodes.summary: Persists the rendered JSON payload back into last_rendered_json for each row after a successful materialisation, giving the next ingest cycle its 3-way-merge base.

nodes.name: _texts_match
nodes.summary: Byte-comparison helper used to short-circuit no-op commits when the newly-rendered content matches what's already on disk.

nodes.name: _semantic_delta
nodes.summary: Structured diff (added/removed/changed counts) used in the state-change-only commit gate so telemetry writers commit only on material change.

nodes.name: materialize_once
nodes.summary: One materialisation cycle: ingest last-rendered snapshots, render all four sources (task_claims, chips, workspace_state, recommendation_log) + dispatcher_control, detect changes via _texts_match/_semantic_delta, write files, commit with phase2b:/phase4: prefixes, and writeback the rendered base. Called on a 2-min timer on the hub.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: parses env config, runs materialize_once in a loop with the configured interval, catches and reports failures without crashing the timer.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Barrel entry point for the ree_core.policy sub-package that re-exports the family of pure-arithmetic policy-layer regulators — NoiseFloor (MECH-313), StructuredCuriosity (MECH-314), TonicVigor (MECH-320), CommitMaintenanceRelease (MECH-342), CommitReadiness (MECH-090 R-c), CandidateRuleField (ARC-063), GatedPolicy (ARC-062), PolicyChunking (ARC-071), PolicyDecomposition (ARC-070), and the newly landed EpistemicDeficitAccumulator (SD-102 / MECH-482). Consumed as the canonical import surface by REEAgent and downstream experiment drivers.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure Python re-export barrel with explicit __all__ list — 13 sub-modules aggregated behind one import namespace; no runtime logic beyond imports.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the claustrum-analog substrate (SD-091 / MECH-481): re-exports the ControlDemandType taxonomy, the two MVP coalition templates, and the CoalitionController primitive, with a docstring documenting the MVP scope and the default-off, bit-identical-when-disabled guarantee.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package barrel using explicit __all__; the module docstring doubles as the SD-091 scope-of-record note.

nodes.name: coalition_controller.py
nodes.summary: Core of the SD-091 coalition/topology control substrate: a non-trainable star-topology controller that opens typed control-demand coalitions from static templates, ticks them toward timeout or completion-condition dissolution, and exposes write_gate/channel_gain multipliers that consumer sites in the agent loop multiply into their existing signals.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure-arithmetic dataclass-based regulator (no nn.Module, no learned parameters); write gates are clamped attenuation-only (<= 1.0) while channel gains may exceed 1.0 -- a deliberate asymmetry documented in the SD-091 design.

nodes.name: coalition_templates.py
nodes.summary: Static COALITION_TEMPLATES registry mapping the two MVP-templated control-demand types (SENSORY_RESAMPLE, PROVENANCE_CHECK) to frozen recruit/suppress/channel-gain weight dictionaries over named consumer targets (E1 encoder, E2 forward model, hippocampal anchor set, BetaGate commitment sites, etc.), with placeholder magnitudes chosen to be numerically distinguishable at every site.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclass template plus a module-level dict registry; the extensive docstring carries the target-name-to-module map that consumer wiring (SD-091 steps 4-5) follows.

nodes.name: control_demand.py
nodes.summary: Declares the 10-class MECH-481 typed control-demand taxonomy as the ControlDemandType enum, of which only SENSORY_RESAMPLE and PROVENANCE_CHECK are templated in the MVP; the other eight members are declared-but-untemplated pending their own consumer substrate.
nodes.languageNotes: Leaf module with zero imports -- the dependency root of the claustrum package.

nodes.name: CoalitionState
nodes.summary: Live state for one open coalition: per-target participating/suppressed weights (re-clamped to [0,1] in __post_init__) and channel gains, plus the per-request lifecycle fields (opened_tick, max_duration_ticks, completion_condition) consulted by coalition_gate and should_dissolve.

nodes.name: CoalitionControllerConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration dataclass for the controller: master enabled switch (default False, bit-identical off), the tuple of templated demand types allowed, the default coalition timeout in ticks, and the global channel-gain scale.

nodes.name: CoalitionController
nodes.summary: The star-topology coalition primitive: request_coalition() instantiates a CoalitionState from a COALITION_TEMPLATES entry, tick() dissolves timed-out or completed coalitions, and write_gate()/channel_gain() compose multipliers across all active coalitions for a named consumer target; recruited_targets/suppressed_targets expose the current topology and reset() clears state on episode boundaries.

nodes.name: CoalitionTemplate
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding the static recruit (participating), suppress, and channel-gain weight dictionaries for one ControlDemandType; consumed by CoalitionController.request_coalition() to build a live CoalitionState, which re-validates the weights itself.

nodes.name: ControlDemandType
nodes.summary: Enum of the ten MECH-481 typed control-demand classes (e.g. sensory resample, provenance check, plus eight declared-but-untemplated members) that key coalition template lookup and the CoalitionController's types_enabled gating.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the REE preservation subsystem, re-exporting the ReconstructionRecord primitives, archive backends, and physical-token exporter that together make a REE organism reconstructable from birth inputs.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package barrel with an explicit __all__ covering all three submodules.

nodes.name: archive.py
nodes.summary: Content-addressed, append-only archive backends (local filesystem, S3-compatible object stores, multi-store replication) with optional client-side AES-256-GCM encryption for storing ReconstructionRecords durably.
nodes.languageNotes: Lazy imports of cryptography and boto3 keep top-level imports stdlib-only; object keys embed the record's sha256 hash, making stores append-only by construction.

nodes.name: reconstruction_record.py
nodes.summary: Defines ReconstructionRecord, an immutable integrity-hashed bundle of the exact inputs (config, seed, environment, provenance, understanding) that deterministically reproduce one REE life, plus faithful REEConfig JSON round-tripping and append-only file persistence.
nodes.languageNotes: Custom dataclass serializer/deserializer preserves tuple-typed config fields that plain JSON would flatten to lists; integrity is a sha256 over canonical (sorted-key, compact-separator) JSON bytes.

nodes.name: token.py
nodes.summary: Physical-token exporter: writes an engravable ~180-byte key line, a gzipped full record, a manifest, a human-readable README, and an optional QR code so a preserved organism survives all-digital failure.
nodes.languageNotes: Stdlib-only at import time; the QR backend (segno or qrcode) is discovered lazily and is optional, with an injectable backend seam for tests.

nodes.name: NoEncryption
nodes.summary: Identity encryptor that stores plaintext JSON; the default Encryptor implementation.

nodes.name: AesGcmEncryptor
nodes.summary: Client-side AES-256-GCM encryptor with key generation, base64 env-var loading, and a nonce-prefixed ciphertext format so the object store only ever sees ciphertext.
nodes.languageNotes: Imports the cryptography package lazily inside the class so the module stays importable without it.

nodes.name: _BaseArchive
nodes.summary: Abstract archive base implementing content-addressed put/load/exists over the record's integrity hash, verifying integrity on both write and read and refusing to overwrite an existing key.

nodes.name: LocalArchive
nodes.summary: Filesystem archive backend writing records atomically (temp file + os.replace) under a local root directory; the hot copy that tests exercise.

nodes.name: S3Archive
nodes.summary: S3-compatible object-store archive backend (intended node 1: Hetzner Object Storage) with lazy boto3 client construction, injectable clients, and head_object-based existence checks.
nodes.languageNotes: boto3 is imported only when no client is injected, keeping ree_core import-light.

nodes.name: MultiArchive
nodes.summary: Replicating wrapper that puts a record into several archives and can verify a record loads with matching integrity from each backend.

nodes.name: s3_archive_from_env
nodes.summary: Factory building an S3Archive from a group-prefixed set of environment variables (endpoint, bucket, credentials), with an injectable client factory for tests.

nodes.name: IntegrityError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when a record's integrity hash fails verification or is malformed.

nodes.name: RecordExistsError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when an append-only write would overwrite an already-stored record.

nodes.name: ReconstructionRecord
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass bundling record_id, seed, serialized config, environment spec, provenance, understanding, lifetime context, schema version, and the sha256 integrity hash of one REE life's birth inputs.

nodes.name: _import_dataclass
nodes.summary: Resolves a dotted ree_core-only path back to a dataclass type during deserialization, refusing anything outside the ree_core namespace.

nodes.name: _ser
nodes.summary: Recursive serializer converting nested dataclasses, tuples, lists, and dicts into JSON-safe structures while recording each dataclass's import path and tuple-ness for faithful round-tripping.

nodes.name: _de
nodes.summary: Recursive deserializer that rebuilds dataclasses and tuple-typed fields from the tagged JSON structures _ser produced.

nodes.name: config_to_dict
nodes.summary: Serializes an REEConfig into a plain JSON-safe dict via the recursive _ser encoder.

nodes.name: config_from_dict
nodes.summary: Rebuilds an REEConfig from its serialized dict, raising if the round-trip does not yield an REEConfig instance.

nodes.name: compute_integrity
nodes.summary: Computes the record's sha256 integrity hash over canonical JSON bytes of every field except the integrity field itself.

nodes.name: verify_integrity
nodes.summary: Returns whether a record's stored integrity string matches a freshly recomputed hash.

nodes.name: capture
nodes.summary: Builds a complete ReconstructionRecord from a live config, seed, environment spec, and caller-supplied provenance, asserting the config round-trips exactly before stamping the integrity hash.

nodes.name: reconstruct_config
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the original REEConfig from a stored record's serialized config dict, the read-side of birth-replay reconstruction.

nodes.name: to_json
nodes.summary: Serializes a ReconstructionRecord to a JSON string.

nodes.name: from_json
nodes.summary: Parses a JSON string back into a ReconstructionRecord dataclass.

nodes.name: write_record
nodes.summary: Persists a verified record to an archive directory atomically (temp file + os.replace), refusing to overwrite an existing record to preserve append-only semantics.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point: loads config/tokens, initialises the DB, and starts the ThreadingHTTPServer.

nodes.name: Handler
nodes.summary: BaseHTTPRequestHandler subclass — the single monolithic request dispatcher for the coordinator HTTP server, routing every GET/POST verb (task-claim, chip-ledger, workspace-state, heartbeat, shutdown, command channel, git-intent, dispatcher-lease) to the corresponding module-level helper after auth_machine validation.

nodes.name: db.py
nodes.summary: Authoritative SQLite persistence layer for the coordinator hub — provides schema migrations, task-claim arbitration (try_open_task_claim), chip ledger, workspace-state / recommendation-log / IGW log queues, git-intent records, dispatcher leases, experiment queue claiming and heartbeats. Every mutation is an atomic transaction serialising cross-session writes.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses sqlite3 with BEGIN IMMEDIATE for arbitration. Every table migration is idempotent (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN guarded).

nodes.name: connect
nodes.summary: Opens a sqlite3 connection with WAL + reasonable defaults and returns it to the caller — the single entry point every reader/writer uses.

nodes.name: _migrate_task_claim_chip_tables
nodes.summary: Idempotent DDL migration for the TASK_CLAIMS + TASK_CHIPS coordinator-authoritative tables (2026-08-28 cutover), including per-resource arbitration rows, chip_ref uniqueness, and the drift log.

nodes.name: upsert_task_claim
nodes.summary: Upsert path for TASK_CLAIMS rows during shadow-sync / registry ingest — writes claim, resources, and derived indexes atomically without arbitration.

nodes.name: upsert_chip
nodes.summary: Upsert path for TASK_CHIPS rows during shadow-sync / registry ingest — merges chip metadata (title/tldr/prompt/status) while preserving history arrays.

nodes.name: reconcile_task_claims

nodes.name: reconcile_chips
nodes.summary: Bulk reconciliation: compares rendered git-side TASK_CHIPS.json against DB rows and logs drift for chips.

nodes.name: log_task_claim_chip_drift
nodes.summary: Records a drift event (claim or chip) into the drift log table for later inspection via task_claim_chip_drift_summary.

nodes.name: task_claim_chip_drift_summary
nodes.summary: Windowed summary of drift events — used by ops dashboards to spot pathological ingest/materialisation loops.

nodes.name: try_open_task_claim
nodes.summary: Atomic arbitration verb — checks for rival active claims on any of the caller's file-shaped resources and either inserts the claim or refuses with exit 3, all inside a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction.

nodes.name: close_task_claim
nodes.summary: Marks a task claim closed with landing commit's committer-date + completion_note; refuses ambiguous session_id lookups and names the disambiguation flag.

nodes.name: renew_task_claim

nodes.name: amend_task_claim

nodes.name: record_chip
nodes.summary: Records a spawned chip in the ledger — enforces the [chip_ref:] prompt marker so the chip can later self-report on completion.

nodes.name: try_claim_chip
nodes.summary: Atomic 'claim' verb for a chip — marks it claimed_by <session> so no other dispatcher starts the same work.

nodes.name: unclaim_chip
nodes.summary: Releases a chip claim, resetting claimed_by so another session may pick it up.

nodes.name: resolve_chip

nodes.name: attach_chip
nodes.summary: Attaches a returned spawn_task task_id to an existing chip row keyed by chip_ref (the only stable identifier available at spawn time).

nodes.name: amend_chip_prompt
nodes.summary: Fixes a chip whose stored prompt lost the [chip_ref:] marker, preserving the broken original in prompt_history.

nodes.name: amend_chip_note
nodes.summary: Amends a chip's claim or resolution note without losing history.

nodes.name: init_db
nodes.summary: One-shot boot helper that opens the DB and runs every migration in dependency order — called from app.main() at startup.

nodes.name: try_claim

nodes.name: release_claim

nodes.name: upsert_experiment
nodes.summary: Upserts an experiment queue row from git-side experiment_queue.json into the coordinator DB during phase3 reconciliation.

nodes.name: upsert_heartbeat

nodes.name: record_shutdown_notice

nodes.name: FieldMappingProvenance

nodes.name: test_task_claim_chip_endpoints.py

nodes.name: TestEndpoints

nodes.name: Base
nodes.summary: Shared fixture — provisions a scratch DB and helpers for opening claims and constructing entries.

nodes.name: stack.py
nodes.summary: Implements the V3 multi-timescale latent stack (L-space), including the SD-005 split encoder (z_self / z_world), the shared beta/theta/delta depth stack, harm/resource/affective-harm encoders, reafference and adversarial-split heads, and the top-level LatentStack module that orchestrates encoding, prediction and precision modulation.
nodes.languageNotes: Large PyTorch nn.Module aggregate (~1,530 non-empty lines). Fifteen exported classes act as sub-modules composed inside LatentStack, gated by a rich config surface (many getattr-with-default lookups on LatentStackConfig).

nodes.name: ReafferencePredictor
nodes.summary: SD-007 / MECH-098 / MECH-101 module that predicts the z_world change caused purely by self-motion (perspective shift) and subtracts it from raw z_world, using the previous z_world_raw plus prior action.

nodes.name: HarmEncoder
nodes.summary: SD-010 dedicated nociceptive encoder (ARC-027) that maps harm observations to z_harm, kept outside the reafference pipeline because harm is never perspective-corrected.

nodes.name: AffectiveHarmEncoder
nodes.summary: SD-011 C-fiber/paleospinothalamic analog (ARC-033) encoding EMA-smoothed harm-proximity observations into z_harm_a and feeding E3 commit gating directly (not counterfactually predicted).

nodes.name: ResourceEncoder
nodes.summary: SD-015 / MECH-112 encoder that maps world observations to z_resource independent of z_world, providing a 'what to seek' signal for GoalState; supports an SD-049 Phase-2 identity classifier head for resource-type discrimination.

nodes.name: HarmForwardModel
nodes.summary: Monolithic harm forward model used prior to the trunk/head refactor, predicting future harm-stream state from current z_harm and action context.

nodes.name: HarmForwardTrunk
nodes.summary: Shared harm-stream feature trunk (ARC-058) consumed by HarmForwardHead and ResidualHarmForward to keep sensory and affective harm predictions on a common representational basis.

nodes.name: HarmForwardHead
nodes.summary: Prediction head on top of HarmForwardTrunk that projects the shared harm features into a per-stream forward prediction (sensory or affective).

nodes.name: ResidualHarmForward
nodes.summary: Residual variant of the harm forward model that composes trunk plus head with a residual connection, letting the head learn only the delta on top of the trunk representation.

nodes.name: HarmBridge
nodes.summary: Bridge module that couples the harm forward model back into the shared latent stack so harm-stream predictions can influence downstream latent updates or E3 commit gating.

nodes.name: _GradReverseFn
nodes.summary: Custom torch.autograd.Function that acts as identity in the forward pass and reverses/scales gradients in the backward pass; used by AdversarialSplitHead for gradient-reversal training.

nodes.name: AdversarialSplitHead
nodes.summary: Adversarial head that uses _GradReverseFn to encourage disentanglement between z_self and z_world, exposing split_losses() so the training loop can add an adversarial cross-prediction penalty.

nodes.name: LatentState
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding one timestep of the latent stack (z_self, z_world, z_beta, z_theta, z_delta, optional harm/affective/resource channels, precision dict, timestamp) with helpers to flatten, move devices, and detach.

nodes.name: SplitEncoder
nodes.summary: SD-005 bottom-up split encoder that maps body observations to z_self and world observations to z_world under top-down conditioning, with optional heads for harm lateral input, event classification, resource-proximity/field supervision and a world-encoder skip connection.

nodes.name: SharedDepthEncoder
nodes.summary: Precision-gated MLP block used to build the shared depth stack (beta -> theta -> delta), taking an input latent plus optional top-down signal and returning encoded features scaled by a learned precision.

nodes.name: LatentStack
nodes.summary: V3 multi-timescale latent-stack nn.Module composing SplitEncoder, SharedDepthEncoder tiers, optional ReafferencePredictor, SelfRecurrenceCell (SELF-1/DR-13), harm/affective/resource encoders, and prediction heads; refuses incoherent iterative-inference configs at construction (F-C4 audit).

nodes.name: test_cloud_scaler_orchestrator_veto.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the cloud-scaler orchestrator veto that prevents shutting down worker boxes with live chip/metaworker sessions or backlog. Covers heartbeat freshness boundaries, role filtering, malformed input handling, and the freshness-window vs commit-cadence invariant.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses tempfile scratch directories per test and constructs heartbeat JSON files on disk to exercise the file-driven veto path exactly as the coordinator sees it.

nodes.name: OrchestratorVetoTest
nodes.summary: Direct unit tests over cs.read_orchestrator: fresh live worker vetoes, stale/malformed/missing heartbeat files do not veto, and filename/role filters (only chip_worker on matching affinity is consulted).

nodes.name: VetoIsWiredIntoTheDecisionLoopTest
nodes.summary: Integration tests that patch cs.run_once and assert that the orchestrator veto actually reaches the shutdown decision path: idle boxes without an orchestrator get shut down, boxes with live workers or declared-but-unrecorded orchestrators are held.

nodes.name: FreshnessWindowCoversTheCommitCadenceTest
nodes.summary: Invariant tests that scan the cloud-scaler source for the ORCH_FRESH_MIN literal and assert it exceeds the writer liveness floor and leaves headroom for git propagation, while remaining bounded so a dead metaworker eventually releases its box.

nodes.name: zworld_p0.py
nodes.summary: SD-070 z_world P0 anti-collapse trainer: buffers world observations then jointly trains the world encoder against scene-structure classification heads (entity presence, distance bucket), proximity/resource-field regressors, reconstruction, preservation, and a variance-covariance penalty to prevent latent collapse.
nodes.languageNotes: PyTorch trainer with dataclass config (ZWorldP0Config); uses torch.Generator with fixed manual_seed for reproducible train/holdout splits and batch sampling on CPU.

nodes.name: chebyshev_offsets
nodes.summary: Builds a tensor of (dy, dx) grid offsets whose Chebyshev (max-norm) distance is <= a fixed radius, used to enumerate candidate cells for entity-distance target computation.

nodes.name: entity_presence_mask
nodes.summary: Returns a boolean mask over grid cells indicating whether a given entity index is present, tolerating either (H, W) or (H, W, C) world observation layouts by unsqueezing/permuting as needed.

nodes.name: scene_structure_targets
nodes.summary: Computes per-entity supervised targets (presence + nearest-distance bucket) for a world observation, using chebyshev_offsets to enumerate candidate cells and bucketing the minimum distance into n_distance_buckets classes.

nodes.name: balanced_class_weights
nodes.summary: Returns per-class weights normalized so present classes contribute equally to cross-entropy, guarding against divide-by-zero and unpresent classes; used to keep rare entity classes trainable.

nodes.name: variance_covariance_penalty
nodes.summary: VICReg-style anti-collapse penalty: hinge on per-dimension standard deviation below variance_gamma plus off-diagonal covariance-squared term, returning both components separately so the trainer can weight them independently.

nodes.name: ZWorldP0Config
nodes.summary: Dataclass carrying all training hyperparameters for ZWorldP0Trainer: loss weights (variance, covariance, presence, distance, proximity, resource-field, reconstruction, preservation), optimizer settings, and seed/holdout controls.

nodes.name: ZWorldP0Trainer
nodes.summary: Buffers world observations plus proximity/resource-field targets and jointly trains the agent's world encoder (plus skip and per-task heads) against scene structure, proximity, resource field, reconstruction, preservation, and VICReg-style anti-collapse losses, reporting holdout metrics.
nodes.languageNotes: Trainer owns its own optimizer and per-task heads (constructed lazily inside train()); relies on the agent's SelfEncoder-like object providing world_encoder, world_precision_logit, and optional world_skip attributes.

nodes.name: agent.py
nodes.summary: The central hub of the REE-v3 substrate: defines REEAgent, a 12k-line nn.Module that wires every architectural component (LatentStack, E1/E2/E3 predictors, HippocampalModule, ResidueField, MultiRateClock, ThetaBuffer, BetaGate, PFC/amygdala/PAG analogs) into the multi-rate SENSE -> E1/E2/E3 tick -> SELECT -> ACT -> RESIDUE -> REPLAY -> OFFLINE loop. Also owns the offline sleep passes (SWS schema installation, REM attribution replay) and the training-loss surface experiments call into.
nodes.languageNotes: A single torch.nn.Module accumulating ~104 methods and a ~2,970-line __init__ that conditionally constructs dozens of optional subsystems behind REEConfig feature flags -- the substrate's god-object by design, since every experiment arm toggles behaviour here.

nodes.name: REEAgent
nodes.summary: The Reflective-Ethical Engine V3 agent. A torch.nn.Module holding all latent streams, predictors, gates and regulators, and enforcing the V3 invariants (residue is persistent and tracks world-delta, E3 is the harm evaluator, E2 trains on motor-sensory error, all replay carries hypothesis_tag=True, precision is E3-derived).

nodes.name: AgentState
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass snapshot of the agent at one timestep: latent state, E3 precision and running variance, step count, accumulated harm, commitment and beta-elevation flags, E3 steps-per-tick, and optional serotonergic state.

nodes.name: candidate_support_preflight
nodes.summary: Diagnostic-only helper computing first-action support metrics (class counts and entropy) across a candidate trajectory set, so callers can decide whether a behavioural interpretation of a selection is admissible.

nodes.name: _resolve_chunk_deliberation_horizon
nodes.summary: Derives the MECH-323 growable chunk ceiling from the agent's rollout budget (HippocampalConfig.horizon), honouring REEConfig.chunk_deliberation_horizon only when explicitly set -- a sentinel default that keeps the knob live instead of silently dead.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Constructs the entire agent: reads REEConfig and conditionally instantiates every latent stream, predictor, gate, regulator and analog module behind feature flags, then initialises all buffers, counters and telemetry state. Roughly 2,970 lines and the single place every experiment arm's configuration is realised.

nodes.name: from_config
nodes.summary: Classmethod convenience constructor that builds a REEConfig via REEConfig.from_dims from raw dimensionalities plus kwargs, then returns the agent.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Resets the agent for a new episode -- flushes the exploration episode buffer, notifies the SleepLoopManager (which may fire a sleep cycle every K episodes), and clears per-episode state. Deliberately does NOT reset the residue field, per the persistence invariant.

nodes.name: sense
nodes.summary: SENSE step: encodes the split observation (body / world / nociceptive / affective-harm / harm-history channels) into the latent stack, updates z_self and z_world, and feeds the many downstream appraisal, salience and gate subsystems. The widest entry point in the loop.

nodes.name: sense_flat
nodes.summary: Backward-compatible SENSE wrapper that splits a single flat observation tensor into body and world channels using configured dims and delegates to sense().

nodes.name: _e1_tick
nodes.summary: E1 tick: refreshes per-stream staleness, optionally gates the latent through the V_s rollout gate, runs the E1 deep predictor and pushes z_self/z_world into the ThetaBuffer (MECH-089). Returns the E1 world-domain prior consumed by the hippocampal proposer.

nodes.name: _e3_tick
nodes.summary: E3 tick: proposes candidate trajectories via HippocampalModule from the theta-cycle summary (never raw z_world, MECH-089), records goal-proximity for the progress-velocity signal, and runs the persistence appraisal.

nodes.name: generate_trajectories
nodes.summary: GENERATE step: re-proposes candidate trajectories only when the E3 tick fires, otherwise returns the cached candidate set (the MECH-057a action-loop gate).

nodes.name: select_action
nodes.summary: SELECT step and the loop's decision core: counts z_goal stream liveness, applies REM precision broadcast recalibration, evaluates E3 scoring with urgency interrupts and commitment latching (MECH-090 trajectory stepping, MECH-091 urgency abort), and returns the action the BetaGate permits to propagate. The single largest method in the substrate.

nodes.name: actor_critic_step
nodes.summary: Runs one actor-critic decision over z_world, applying the co-shaping ablation lever (live z_world lets gradients reach the encoder; detached z_world reproduces the refuted frozen-latent arm). Returns the graph-connected ActorCriticStep the PPO update consumes.

nodes.name: act
nodes.summary: Complete V3 REE action loop over a flat observation: sense_flat -> clock advance -> E1 tick -> generate -> select -> optional quiescent-cycle replay, incrementing the step counter and returning the action tensor.

nodes.name: act_with_log_prob
nodes.summary: Action-loop variant that also returns the log-probability of the sampled action, for policy-gradient style drivers.

nodes.name: _do_replay
nodes.summary: MECH-092 sharp-wave-ripple-equivalent replay fired on quiescent E3 cycles. All replay content carries hypothesis_tag=True so it can never accumulate residue; when serotonin is enabled the drive state biases start-point selection.

nodes.name: update_residue
nodes.summary: RESIDUE step: accumulates ethical residue at the current z_world location scaled by the SD-003 world-delta attribution, blocked entirely by hypothesis_tag (MECH-094) or by harm that is not agent-owned.

nodes.name: record_transition
nodes.summary: Records a detached (z_self_t, action, z_self_t+1) triple into the E2 transition buffer for motor-sensory forward-model training; detaching is required to keep E3's graph out of the E2 backward pass.

nodes.name: record_executed_action
nodes.summary: Lets drivers that step the environment directly (bypassing select_action) tell the agent which action actually ran, so the E1 action-conditioning buffer is not silently filled with zero vectors -- the failure mode that makes an 'ON' ablation arm scientifically vacuous.

nodes.name: compute_prediction_loss
nodes.summary: E1 world-model prediction loss: samples a horizon-length window from the paired self/world experience buffers, builds the combined sequence, runs E1 and restores the saved hidden state afterwards.

nodes.name: update_z_goal
nodes.summary: MECH-112 wanting update: seeds and updates z_goal from the benefit signal, preferring z_resource (object-type latent) over z_world under SD-015, and under SD-057 sourcing the seed from the most-wanted object's stored embedding via the per-type incentive token bank.

nodes.name: serotonin_step
nodes.summary: MECH-203 tonic serotonin update: reads the z_harm_a norm from the current latent, advances tonic 5-HT, and writes the resulting seeding gain and wanting floor into GoalConfig so goal updates use dynamic serotonergic values.

nodes.name: update_benefit_salience
nodes.summary: MECH-203 SR-2: tags the current residue-field location with benefit salience via the SD-014 valence/wanting channel, routed through incentive-sensitized amplification when that lever is enabled.

nodes.name: update_harm_salience
nodes.summary: Harm-side counterpart to update_benefit_salience: writes harm salience into the residue field's valence vector at the current z_world position.

nodes.name: compute_e2_loss
nodes.summary: E2 motor-sensory forward-model loss in the z_self domain, sampled as a random minibatch from the transition buffer.

nodes.name: offline_integration
nodes.summary: Offline integration pass: replays the feature-axis-concatenated self/world experience through E1 with the aligned action history, then integrates the residue field, returning merged metrics.

nodes.name: note_task_outcome
nodes.summary: Records a scalar task outcome into the agent's outcome tracking, feeding the readiness and appraisal signals that gate commitment.

nodes.name: run_sws_schema_pass
nodes.summary: SD-017 SWS-analog pass: installs differentiated context attractors in E1.ContextMemory by writing compressed z_world prototypes sampled from recent waking experience -- the MECH-166 slot-formation phase that REM slot-filling depends on.

nodes.name: run_rem_attribution_pass
nodes.summary: SD-017 REM-analog pass: replays recent trajectory experience through the hippocampal module forwards and in reverse, evaluating residue terrain per segment with hypothesis_tag=True so no new residue accrues -- the MECH-166 slot-filling phase.

nodes.name: run_sleep_cycle
nodes.summary: Convenience driver for a complete SWS -> REM sleep cycle: enters each mode, runs its pass, exits, and returns merged metrics. No-op when both sws_enabled and rem_enabled are false.

nodes.name: _assemble_control_vector
nodes.summary: Assembles the read-only ControlVector telemetry for the current E3 tick -- V_outcome, C_effort (dACC EVC), C_time and G_vigor -- logging the shared MECH-320 v_t explicitly so the C_time/G_vigor collapse is computable from a manifest. Purely observational.

nodes.name: get_state
nodes.summary: Builds an AgentState snapshot from the live agent -- latent state, E3 precision and running variance, step count, episode harm, commitment and beta flags, clock rate, and serotonin state when enabled.

nodes.name: forward
nodes.summary: nn.Module forward hook -- delegates straight to act(), so the agent can be called like any torch module.

nodes.name: module.py
nodes.summary: Implements HippocampalModule, the V3 CEM trajectory proposer that searches action-object space (SD-004) and emits value-flat candidate trajectories for E3 to weight (ARC-007 strict). Also hosts replay, reverse replay, novelty/visitation bookkeeping, anchor sets, staleness accumulation and ghost-goal ranking.
nodes.languageNotes: A single ~4100-line torch nn.Module class with 73 methods; most mechanism switches are read off HippocampalConfig rather than constructor arguments.

nodes.name: visitation.py
nodes.summary: Defines VisitationCounter, an unconditionally-allocated per-region visit-count tracker over a fixed-size FIFO anchor buffer in z_world. Deliberately distinct from FamiliarityTracker (an EMA) and the agent's raw visitation buffer, and kept out of scoring paths apart from one documented MECH-057b read.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors FamiliarityTracker's nearest-anchor kernel shape but stores exact counts; the module docstring records an explicit invariant about permitted consumers.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Central configuration surface for the whole REE-v3 agent: sixteen per-subsystem dataclasses plus the master REEConfig, its master-flag resolvers and the from_dims factory that every experiment builds its agent from.
nodes.languageNotes: Dataclass-based configuration with hundreds of default-off feature flags; __post_init__ acts as an OR-only master-flag resolver so a single switch can light a whole mechanism cluster.

nodes.name: HippocampalModule
nodes.summary: The hippocampal planner: proposes candidate trajectories by CEM search over E2 action-object space, scores them value-flat, and exposes replay, credit-sweep, anchor-set and ghost-goal machinery to the agent loop.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Builds the module from a HippocampalConfig plus the E2 predictor and residue field, allocating the terrain prior, familiarity and visitation trackers, event segmenter, anchor set and ghost-goal bank according to the configured flags.

nodes.name: propose_trajectories
nodes.summary: Core CEM loop: samples action-object candidates around the terrain prior, rolls them out through E2, scores and re-fits an elite set, and returns value-flat trajectories together with diagnostics.

nodes.name: _score_trajectory
nodes.summary: Scores one candidate trajectory from residue-field terrain, curiosity bonus and horizon terms, optionally returning the component breakdown for diagnostics.

nodes.name: _curiosity_bonus
nodes.summary: Computes the SD-025 curiosity term for a rolled-out world sequence from the familiarity tracker, contributing a novelty-seeking component to the trajectory score.

nodes.name: compute_novelty_score
nodes.summary: Returns a novelty score for a z_world point as the complement of tracked familiarity, used as the curiosity signal and as telemetry.

nodes.name: update_familiarity
nodes.summary: Writes a visited z_world point into the proximity-weighted familiarity EMA, gated on the waking phase so replay does not inflate familiarity.

nodes.name: record_visitation
nodes.summary: Increments the unconditional VisitationCounter for a visited z_world region during waking steps, supplying exact visit counts to fishtank telemetry.

nodes.name: _compute_mode_noise_scale
nodes.summary: Maps the current operating mode onto a multiplier for CEM proposal noise, widening or narrowing the search distribution by mode.

nodes.name: _compute_mode_horizon_scale
nodes.summary: Maps the current operating mode onto a planning-horizon multiplier, so modes plan further ahead or shorter as configured.

nodes.name: _build_chunk_candidates
nodes.summary: Assembles candidate action chunks from the registered chunk source, seeding the CEM population with reusable multi-step fragments rather than only fresh samples.

nodes.name: _apply_policy_decomposition
nodes.summary: Applies the configured decomposition source to chunk candidates, expanding them into sub-goal tiles and applying the harm penalty before they re-enter the candidate pool.

nodes.name: replay
nodes.summary: MECH-092 quiescent replay: re-runs recent theta-buffer content through the module during heartbeat downtime, tagged as hypothesis so it cannot produce residue.

nodes.name: reverse_replay
nodes.summary: Replays a committed trajectory backwards from its outcome, the substrate used for reverse-order credit assignment and wanting spread.

nodes.name: diverse_replay
nodes.summary: Mode- and bias-aware replay sampler that draws a spread of stored trajectories rather than the most recent ones, feeding the offline consolidation pathway.

nodes.name: compute_completion_signal
nodes.summary: Derives an aggregate action-loop completion signal across a set of candidate trajectories for the MECH-057 gate.

nodes.name: verify_sequence_completion
nodes.summary: Scores a candidate trajectory's sequence-completion confidence for the MECH-057b promotion gate, reading the visitation counter read-only when the gate flag is enabled.

nodes.name: promote_candidates
nodes.summary: Filters and promotes scored candidate trajectories into the set handed onward for commitment, applying completion and support-preserving gates.

nodes.name: backward_credit_sweep
nodes.summary: Propagates an outcome-quality signal backwards along the committed trajectory, assigning credit to the states and action objects that led to it.

nodes.name: build_goal_payload
nodes.summary: Packages the current latent, goal, residue and amygdala-derived state into the goal payload consumed downstream, respecting simulation mode.

nodes.name: rank_ghost_goals
nodes.summary: Ranks banked ghost goals against the current goal using the persistence appraisal, deciding which abandoned goal is most worth resuming.

nodes.name: forward
nodes.summary: nn.Module entry point that delegates to propose_trajectories with the same mode-conditioned arguments.

nodes.name: VisitationCounter
nodes.summary: Proximity-bucketed visit counter over a fixed-size FIFO anchor buffer in z_world, allocated unconditionally so visit counts are always available as telemetry.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Allocates the anchor buffer, per-anchor count vector and FIFO cursor for the configured world dimension, anchor count and kernel bandwidth.

nodes.name: _nearest_active
nodes.summary: Finds the nearest allocated anchor to a query point and its distance, the shared primitive behind both query and update.

nodes.name: query
nodes.summary: Returns the recorded visit count for the region containing a z_world point, or zero when no anchor lies within the bandwidth. Read-only.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Increments the count for the nearest in-bandwidth anchor, allocating a fresh anchor (overwriting the oldest when full) on first visit to a region.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Clears all anchors and counts back to the empty state, used between episodes or runs.

nodes.name: derive_stdlib_rng_seed
nodes.summary: Derives a per-stream stdlib RNG seed from a base seed, so independent random streams stay reproducible and decorrelated.

nodes.name: _observed_config_registry
nodes.summary: Lazily creates and returns the process-wide registry of observed REEConfig instances stored on the sys module.

nodes.name: _register_observed_config
nodes.summary: Announces a freshly-constructed REEConfig to the provenance registry, honouring a suppression flag and a hard cap, and never raising so config construction cannot break.

nodes.name: REEConfig
nodes.summary: Master configuration dataclass composing every subsystem config plus device, seed and several hundred mechanism flags; its resolvers and factories are the single construction path for a V3 agent.

nodes.name: __post_init__
nodes.summary: Master-flag resolver: OR-only expansion of convenience flags (MECH-307 conjunction, sleep-aggregation cluster, MECH-090 readiness) into their sub-flags, then records the resolved config in the provenance registry.

nodes.name: enable_sleep_aggregation_cluster
nodes.summary: Convenience preset (GAP-3) that flips the eight sleep-phase flags true so the offline consolidation pathway runs end to end from a single switch; OR-only and returns self for chaining.

nodes.name: enable_goal_stream
nodes.summary: Turns on the goal-stream cluster and sets its weighting parameters (goal weight, wanting weight, benefit threshold, drive weight) in one call.

nodes.name: from_dims
nodes.summary: Primary factory: builds a fully wired REEConfig from observation/action/latent dimensions plus several hundred keyword feature switches, propagating each into the right subsystem config.
nodes.languageNotes: Keyword-only feature flags default to off; unknown kwargs are not rejected here, so a new knob must be threaded through every call site explicitly.

nodes.name: goal_stream
nodes.summary: Named preset constructor producing a from_dims config with the goal-stream cluster already enabled.

nodes.name: large
nodes.summary: Named preset constructor producing a larger-capacity latent/predictor configuration from the same three base dimensions.

nodes.name: xlarge
nodes.summary: Named preset constructor for the largest standard capacity tier, scaling latent and predictor widths above the `large` preset.

nodes.name: LatentStackConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the latent stack: z_self / z_world / harm-stream dimensions, encoder options and the alpha mixing coefficients that govern latent updates.

nodes.name: E1Config
nodes.summary: Configuration for the E1 world-domain prior predictor, including its heads, auxiliary losses and the resource/event options layered on top of it.

nodes.name: E2Config
nodes.summary: Configuration for the E2 fast predictor and its action-object space, which the hippocampal CEM search rolls trajectories out through.

nodes.name: E3Config
nodes.summary: Configuration for the E3 selector, which applies all value weighting to hippocampal proposals; by far the largest subsystem config, carrying the selection, authority and modulatory-bias flags.

nodes.name: EventSegmenterScaleConfig
nodes.summary: Per-scale parameters for one timescale of the event segmenter, such as its surprise threshold and boundary refractory behaviour.

nodes.name: EventSegmenterConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the multi-scale event segmenter that emits boundary events consumed by the hippocampal module.

nodes.name: InvalidationTriggerConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the invalidation trigger that marks regions of the hippocampal map stale when predictions break down.

nodes.name: AnchorSetConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the MECH-269 anchor set: how many anchors are held, how they are selected and ticked, and the thresholds governing their turnover.

nodes.name: StalenessAccumulatorConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the staleness accumulator that integrates per-region and per-stream staleness over time.

nodes.name: GhostGoalBankConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the ghost-goal bank: capacity, decay and ranking parameters for abandoned goals that may later be resumed.

nodes.name: PersistenceAppraisalComputeConfig
nodes.summary: Small configuration bundle controlling how the persistence appraisal used in ghost-goal ranking is computed.

nodes.name: HippocampalConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration consumed directly by HippocampalModule: CEM population and horizon, mode-conditioning scales, familiarity bandwidth, replay options and the promotion-gate flags.

nodes.name: ResidueConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the residue field whose curvature in z_world supplies the terrain the hippocampal search navigates.

nodes.name: HeartbeatConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the E3 heartbeat cycle, including the quiescent intervals during which replay and offline consolidation run.

nodes.name: EnvironmentConfig
nodes.summary: Small configuration block describing the environment an agent is run against.

nodes.name: bla.py
nodes.summary: SD-035 basolateral-amygdala analogue: converts the z_harm_a affective stream into arousal-dependent hippocampal encoding gain (MECH-074a inverted-U), a content-selective per-trace retrieval bias vector (MECH-074b), and a harm-prediction-error remap signal gated by predictor attribution (MECH-074d). Peer module to the low-latency CeA analogue, operating on the hippocampal map rather than scalar salience channels.
nodes.languageNotes: Self-contained dataclass-config + stateful analogue pattern: BLAConfig (tuning constants sourced from cited neuroscience literature), BLAOutput (per-tick result record), and BLAAnalog (the stepping module). No project-internal imports, so the module is a leaf in the dependency graph.

nodes.name: BLAConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration record holding every BLA tuning constant: the inverted-U encoding-gain envelope (encoding_gain_max, encoding_gain_floor, arousal_threshold_on, arousal_peak), the post-event decay window, the retrieval-bias alpha and compensation terms, and the remap PE sigma threshold with its attribution gate.

nodes.name: BLAOutput
nodes.summary: Per-tick result record emitted by BLAAnalog.tick, carrying encoding_gain, the encoding-time arousal_tag, the per-trace retrieval_bias vector, the remap_signal, and the harm-PE diagnostics (magnitude, running baseline std, remaining encoding-window steps).

nodes.name: BLAAnalog
nodes.summary: Stateful basolateral-amygdala analogue stepped once per agent.sense(). Tracks harm-PE running statistics, the post-event encoding window, and emits encoding gain, arousal tagging, retrieval bias and remap decisions consumed by the hippocampal write and readout paths.

nodes.name: BLAAnalog.__init__
nodes.summary: Constructs the BLA analogue from an optional BLAConfig, validating and caching the arousal-threshold and inverted-U envelope parameters before delegating to reset for the mutable running state.

nodes.name: BLAAnalog.reset
nodes.summary: Clears all mutable per-episode state: the harm-PE running mean and standard deviation, the last encoding gain and arousal tag, and the remaining post-event encoding-window step counter.

nodes.name: BLAAnalog.tick
nodes.summary: Main per-step entry point: reads the z_harm_a affective stream and its one-step prediction, computes the inverted-U arousal-dependent encoding gain and its decay window, builds the content-selective per-trace retrieval bias vector from arousal tags, updates the harm-PE EMA baseline, and decides the attribution-gated remap signal before packaging everything into a BLAOutput.
nodes.languageNotes: Returns an early no-op BLAOutput (encoding_gain exactly 1.0) below arousal_threshold_on, which is the module's backward-compatibility contract when the feature flag is on but arousal is subthreshold.

nodes.name: BLAAnalog.diagnostics
nodes.summary: Returns the module's current internal counters (encoding-window steps remaining and related integer state) for experiment manifests and contract assertions.

tour.title: REEAgent Orchestrator
tour.description: REE V3 has no main.py -- the REEAgent class in ree_core/agent.py is the runtime entry point that wires every substrate together into a single cognitive cycle: sense -> E1/E2/E3 predict -> select -> act -> actor-critic training -> offline replay. This file is the map of the whole system: reading its constructor tells you which subsystems exist, and reading step() tells you the order they fire in. Every other tour step will drill into a subsystem that agent.py imports and composes here.
tour.languageLesson: REE uses Python composition (not inheritance) as the architectural glue: REEAgent holds concrete instances of each subsystem (E1, E2, E3, HippocampalModule, ...) as attributes, and orchestrates them by explicit method calls rather than framework magic. This makes every dataflow readable in one file and every substrate independently swappable behind a config flag.

tour.title: Central Substrate Configuration
tour.description: REEConfig in ree_core/utils/config.py is the second-most-imported file in the codebase (fan-in 12) and the reason experiments can be rerun byte-identically months later: every subsystem carries a nested dataclass here with its default flags, and the observed-config registry snapshots the exact resolved config into each run manifest. When the tour later mentions an SD-xxx or MECH-xxx flag, it is toggled through a field defined in this file.
tour.languageLesson: Python dataclasses (with field defaults and frozen=False) give you serialisable configuration objects with almost no ceremony; REE combines them with an observed-config registry that records which knobs a given run actually read, so a claim's evidence trail can be reconstructed from the manifest alone.

tour.title: Latent Space and Goal Representations
tour.description: REE's central architectural commitment is a split latent space: z_self (bodily / capacity state), z_world (external causal state), and parallel harm-anticipation and harm-suffering streams. ree_core/latent/stack.py defines every encoder plus the LatentStack that anchors SD-005 self/world separation, SD-010/SD-011 dual harm streams, and MECH-269 per-stream value signals. ree_core/goal.py sits alongside it as a slow-decay attractor in z_world plus the SD-057 incentive-salience token bank -- goals are represented in the same space the world model predicts in, which is why the tour will later meet goal-directed E3 selection rather than a bolt-on reward function.

tour.title: E1: Persistent Predictive Context
tour.description: E1 is the long-horizon predictor: an LSTM transition model over the latent stack, plus a 16-slot cue-indexed ContextMemory (MECH-152) and the SD-016 cue-context / action / terrain heads. Its job is to keep temporal coherence across many steps so the fast predictor and the selector below inherit a stable context rather than reasoning from a single-step snapshot. The MECH-216 schema readout is what lets downstream substrates read 'what E1 currently expects' rather than only 'what E1 predicts next'.

tour.title: E2: Fast Forward Modelling and Rollouts
tour.description: Where E1 tracks context, E2 rolls out candidate futures: self and world forward models with contrastive next-state losses (SD-056), counterfactual rollouts, and the E2_world single-pass comparator that gives z_world its own agency-conditioned prediction stream (SD-031). The uncertainty head (SD-063) attaches a quantile predictive-uncertainty channel that E3 later reads to downweight over-confident trajectories. E2 is the source of the candidate trajectories that Step 6 will score and commit to.

tour.title: E3: Trajectory Selection and Commitment
tour.description: E3 is where architectural claims about care, harm, and commitment become mechanism. e3_selector.py scores E2 rollouts against harm, benefit, goal and residue costs, arbitrates a dual-system F/B eligibility envelope with go/no-go gating, and commits an action under precision-scaled thresholds -- meaning viability concerns affect the state the agent commits from, not a post-hoc safety filter. The 2026-09-07 landing of MECH-439's channel-commensurability operator (rung 3 of the f_dominance conversion ceiling) lives here, and the diversity head keeps E3 from degenerating to single-mode selection.

tour.title: Hippocampal Trajectory Proposal and Replay
tour.description: The hippocampal cluster is where E2's rollouts get their proposals and where the residue signals from Step 8 come back as credit assignment. module.py orchestrates event segmentation, anchor sets, ghost goals, visitation, staleness, curiosity and replay; anchor_set.py stores scale-tagged MECH-269 anchors with dual-trace preservation; ghost_goal_bank.py ranks those anchors as MECH-292 ghost goals for waking probe search; staleness_accumulator.py is the leaky integrator that keeps stale goals from dominating the bank. Together they are the source of the trajectory diversity that E3 depends on.

tour.title: Residue Field and Suffering Accumulator
tour.description: REE's care-from-empathy framing is grounded here. The residue field is an RBF-backed distributed representation of residual salience and care markers -- consequences of past actions that persist and shape future selection (INV-001). Alongside it, the MECH-219 harm-suffering accumulator is a hysteretic integrator that converts the medium-timescale unpleasantness channel into a slow, controllability-gated suffering load state (z_harm_suffering) rather than a per-step penalty. Both are read by E3 in Step 6, closing the loop between what happened and what will be committed to next.

tour.title: Cingulate, PFC, and Policy-Layer Regulators
tour.description: These four package barrels expose the control plane surrounding E3. The cingulate cluster (SD-032: dACC, AIC, pACC, PCC, salience coordinator, stuck-state detector) implements adaptive-control and salience gating. The PFC package (frontopolar, lateral-PFC, OFC, escape-affordance linker/bridge) hosts commitment-release levers including the SD-033e frontopolar de-commit. The policy package assembles pure-arithmetic regulators (NoiseFloor MECH-313, StructuredCuriosity MECH-314, TonicVigor MECH-320, CommitReadiness MECH-090 R-c, GatedPolicy ARC-062) and the regulators package holds the GABAergic decay, phasic surprise, broadcast-override, and simulation-mode rule-gate siblings that shape E3's inputs.
tour.languageLesson: Python __init__.py barrel files re-export a subpackage's public surface so callers can write 'from ree_core.policy import GatedPolicy' rather than reaching into internal file paths. In REE this is load-bearing: the barrel is the stable import contract, so an SD-* implementation can be split across new files inside the package without breaking every caller.

tour.title: Sleep, Consolidation, and Serotonergic Modulation
tour.description: Sleep is a first-class V3 mechanism, not a V4 deferral. The sleep package barrel wires the phase manager, routing gate, MECH-275 Bayesian aggregator, MEL consumer, cross-module consolidator, self-model aggregator, replay sampler and onset gate into the offline pass. Alongside it, serotonin.py implements the MECH-203/204 tonic-5HT state variable that provides benefit / harm salience tagging and REM zero-point recalibration -- without it, all SWS replay would be harm-biased (the depressive-consolidation asymmetry that motivated pulling this substrate into V3).

tour.title: The Coordination Plane: Hub, DB, and Sync Daemon
tour.description: REE V3 runs experiments across a fleet (Mac + Hetzner cloud workers), and the coordinator subsystem is what keeps that fleet coherent. PLAN.md is the plan-of-record; coordinator/app.py is a pure-stdlib HTTP hub exposing claim arbitration, chip ledger, heartbeat/status ingest, and manifest spool endpoints; coordinator/db.py (fan-in 28 -- the most-depended-upon file in the graph) is the SQLite storage layer with the WAL + BEGIN IMMEDIATE atomic claim gate that serialises concurrent claimants; sync_daemon.py is the Phase 3 sole git writer that turns DB state into commits under REE_assembly. This is how experiment results get from a worker to the evidence record without racing.

tour.title: Coordinator Schema: The Data Contract
tour.description: The whole coordination plane in Step 11 rests on the SQL schema in coordinator/schema.sql, applied idempotently at coordinator startup. Three tables show how the pieces fit: experiments and results are the authoritative queue-and-outcome pair (results is what sync_daemon materialises into REE_assembly manifests); task_claims is the arbitration table that atomic BEGIN IMMEDIATE inserts against, and it is the durable form of every 'task_claim.py open' call a session makes anywhere in the fleet. If you understand this schema you can read every operator alert and every phase3 audit.
tour.languageLesson: SQL migrations should be idempotent (safe to re-run) and additive (never drop columns downstream code still reads). REE applies schema.sql on every coordinator startup using CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN patterns, so a rolling hub restart never requires a migration step and an older sync_daemon binary keeps working while a newer one adds fields.
